name: Cosmology: universal luminosity-distance quadrature
description: Discover an eight-node positive quadrature rule for dimensionless luminosity distance in spatially flat, time-varying dark-energy models. The same nodes and weights must work across all models. Minimize the worst relative error against independent adaptive integration on disjoint public validation cosmologies. This is a locally designed synthetic numerical-method task reconstructed from published distance and CPL equations.

sources.locator: Hogg, Distance measures in cosmology, v4; sections 4, 5 and 7, equations 15, 16 and 21: comoving and luminosity distance.
Linder, Exploring the Expansion History of the Universe; section B, equations 6 and 7 and following density evolution: w(a)=w0+wa(1-a).

sources.title: Quadrature algorithms to the luminosity distance with a time-dependent dark energy model
sources.locator: Develops and compares Romberg and Gaussian quadrature for luminosity distance in CPL dark-energy models. The fixed universal eight-node rule and public cosmology split are local restrictions on that same numerical-method problem.

limitations: Local reduced benchmark, not original paper code, measurements, or a reproduction of a published benchmark score.
Assumes a flat matter plus smooth CPL dark-energy background; omits radiation, spatial curvature and neutrino effects.
The calibration and validation cosmologies are disjoint but public; repeated optimization against validation can overfit this finite suite.
The metric tests numerical accuracy at fixed eight-sample inference cost, not measured speed or a resolution of the dark-energy problem.

name: Cosmology: compact dark-energy growth approximation
description: Improve a six-coefficient growth-index formula for the linear growth rate and normalized growth factor in smooth CPL dark-energy cosmologies. A tightly integrated general-relativistic second-order ODE provides an independent numerical reference. The score is the worst relative error across both observables on disjoint public validation cosmologies, extending the constant-gamma seed within a fixed compact ansatz.

sources.locator: Linder and Cahn, Parameterized Beyond-Einstein Growth; equations 1-3 and 8: growth-index ansatz and GR growth equation; equations 14-15: constant growth-index approximation.
Linder, Exploring the Expansion History of the Universe; equations 6 and 7 and following density evolution define the CPL background.

limitations: Local synthetic approximation task, not an observational discovery or reproduction of a paper's fitted coefficients.
Uses general relativity, flat space and smooth dark energy; excludes nonlinear structure, modified gravity, radiation and neutrino effects.
The numerical reference uses the explicitly specified finite matter-era boundary D(ai)=D_x(ai)=ai at ai=0.001; it is not a full Boltzmann cosmology solver.
Calibration and validation models are disjoint but public. Better scores establish accuracy only on this finite model set and do not resolve the dark-energy problem.

name: Expansion-history models fitted to the Pantheon+ supernova Hubble diagram
description: Propose a parametric expansion history E(z) = H(z)/H0 with at most six parameters and fit it to the 1,580 Pantheon+ Type Ia supernova light curves with zHD > 0.01 (the 1,590-object cosmology sample minus the ten Cepheid-host calibrators) (corrected apparent magnitudes and the full statistical plus systematic covariance). The absolute magnitude is profiled analytically; the score is the minimum chi-squared, lower is better. Flat LambdaCDM with a fitted matter density is reported for comparison.

sources.locator: Brout et al. 2022, The Pantheon+ Analysis: Cosmological Constraints; Section 2 (data), Section 3 (likelihood with the STAT+SYS covariance, zHD > 0.01 cut).
Pantheon+SH0ES.dat and Pantheon+SH0ES_STAT+SYS.cov, fetched by scripts/prepare_science_data.py and pinned by SHA-256.

limitations: Real measurements: the data are the public Pantheon+ release, fetched at prepare time (network), not redistributed.
The likelihood profiles the absolute magnitude and fixes H0 = 70 for the distance scale, so only the shape of E(z) is constrained; the SH0ES Cepheid calibrators are excluded.

A lower chi-squared than LambdaCDM with more parameters is not by itself evidence for new physics; model comparison needs an information criterion or Bayesian evidence, which the evaluator reports the ingredients for (chi-squared and parameter count).
